summary: This work demonstrates Rabi-Driven Reset (RDR), a measurement-free continuous cooling protocol for a superconducting cavity mode that achieves single-photon decay in $1.2$ µs (170× faster than the intrinsic $170$ µs lifetime) and cools $\sim 30$ thermal photons to $\bar{n} = 0.045 \pm 0.025$ in $80$ µs. The method combines a strong Rabi drive on a transmon qubit with sideband drives on memory and readout modes detuned by the Rabi frequency to convert dispersive coupling into effective Jaynes–Cummings interactions, creating engineered dissipation that scales with qubit-mode coupling rather than intermode cross-Kerr.
motivation: High-Q bosonic memories essential for hardware-efficient quantum error correction are isolated from the environment, creating a bottleneck for fast reset—existing methods either rely on weak cross-Kerr conversion or measurement-based sequences with substantial latency.
method: A strong resonant Rabi drive ($\Omega_R / 2\pi = 9$ MHz) on a transmon qubit ($\omega_q / 2\pi = 6.33$ GHz, $E_C / 2\pi = 265$ MHz, $T_1 = 25$ µs) is applied together with sideband drives on a memory cavity ($\omega_m / 2\pi = 6.914$ GHz, $\kappa_m^{-1} = 170$ µs, $2\chi_m / 2\pi = 57$ kHz) and readout mode ($\omega_r / 2\pi = 7.7$ GHz, $\kappa_r / 2\pi = 0.382$ MHz, $2\chi_r / 2\pi = 0.635$ MHz) detuned by $\Omega_R$ to engineer dissipation without measurement.
result: Maximum cooling rates of $d\bar{n}/dt = -0.73 \pm 0.08$ MHz (at $\bar{a}_m \chi_m = \kappa/2$) are achieved, limited by the readout linewidth; a single Fock state is cooled to vacuum with 93% fidelity, and the coupling rate scales with the dispersive interaction independently of intermode cross-Kerr, enabling fast cooling in weakly coupled architectures.
